facts.text: Ramos traces its origins to mid-eighteenth-century Spanish colonial ranching outposts established along the northern bank of the Rio Grande.
Early settlers in Ramos were often descendants of colonists from Nuevo Santander who focused on pastoral activities and livestock operations.
The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo in 1848 definitively established the Rio Grande as the border, ending years of instability for Ramos.
Ramos features a semi-arid climate with hot summers and mild winters, typical of the Lower Rio Grande Valley region.
The landscape of Ramos is dominated by brushland and semi-arid scrub, supporting sparse vegetation adapted to dry conditions.
Proximity to the Rio Grande shapes the local hydrology of Ramos, influencing groundwater recharge and seasonal water availability.
